name: Woolly Hair

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Woolly Hair

criteria.description: Presence of tightly coiled, fine, and brittle hair with a woolly appearance
Abnormal hair growth pattern with patchy or diffuse involvement
Presence or absence of associated cardiac abnormalities (e.g., arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy)
Positive family history of woolly hair or related syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (woolly hair texture and abnormal hair growth pattern) with or without minor/supportive criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis, especially to identify syndromic forms.

laboratory: Hair shaft microscopy showing twisted, oval, or flattened hair shafts
Genetic testing identifying mutations in plakoglobin (JUP), desmoplakin (DSP), or other desmosomal proteins
imaging: Echocardiography or cardiac MRI to assess for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
other: Trichoscopy revealing characteristic hair shaft abnormalities
Skin biopsy in syndromic cases showing palmoplantar keratoderma

distinguishingFeatures: Hair is dry, frizzy, and unmanageable but not tightly coiled
Hair shaft shows triangular or heart-shaped cross-section
Hair shafts twisted 180 degrees along their axis

redFlags: Signs of cardiac arrhythmia or syncope
Rapid progression of hair loss or scalp inflammation
Family history of sudden cardiac death
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.

McKoy G, Protonotarios N, Crosby A, et al. Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease). Lancet. 2000.
